title: Build a cross-platform UI factory
description: A UI toolkit needs to create buttons and checkboxes that look native on each platform. The Mac and Windows component classes already exist. Wire up a UIFactory interface and two concrete factories — MacUIFactory and WindowsUIFactory — then complete the Application class that uses whichever factory it receives.
hints: UIFactory is an interface with createButton() and createCheckbox() methods
MacUIFactory returns MacButton and MacCheckbox; WindowsUIFactory returns their Windows counterparts
Application stores the factory and calls it — it never mentions a concrete platform class
issues: Application directly instantiates platform-specific components, making it impossible to swap platforms without editing its code
Adding a new platform requires touching every place that creates components
overallGoal: Use the Abstract Factory pattern so Application can build a complete UI family without knowing which platform it is running on.
goals: Define a UIFactory interface with createButton() and createCheckbox() methods
Implement MacUIFactory and WindowsUIFactory, each returning the correct platform-specific components
Update Application to depend only on UIFactory — never reference Mac or Windows classes directly
